source_refs.quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession
These three expressions deal with different concepts and apply to different circumstances.

In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet.
In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.
there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession
The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession
If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself

source_refs.quote: That the respondent has sub-let the Shop in question to one Shri Kapil Luthra S/o Shri Veer Bhan @ Rs.5500/- p.m. without the knowledge, consent or permission of the petitioner.
Moreover, the sub letee namely Shri Kapil Luthra is using a shop in question as Godown and has taken exclusive possession of the shop in question.

nodes.text: Respondent

source_refs.quote: the respondent

nodes.text: Shri Kapil Luthra

source_refs.quote: Shri Kapil Luthra

nodes.text: Petitioner

source_refs.quote: the petitioner

nodes.text: The petitioner alleges that the respondent sub-let the shop to Kapil Luthra at Rs.5500 per month without the petitioner's knowledge, consent, or permission

source_refs.quote: That the respondent has sub-let the Shop in question to one Shri Kapil Luthra S/o Shri Veer Bhan @ Rs.5500/- p.m. without the knowledge, consent or permission of the petitioner.

nodes.text: The petitioner alleges that Kapil Luthra uses the shop as a godown and has exclusive possession of it

source_refs.quote: Moreover, the sub letee namely Shri Kapil Luthra is using a shop in question as Godown and has taken exclusive possession of the shop in question.

nodes.text: The respondent denies having sublet the shop to Kapil Luthra at Rs.5500 per month

source_refs.quote: It is denied by the respondent that the answering respondent has sublet the shop in question to Sh. Kapil Luthra, S/o Sh. Virbhan @ Rs.5500/- p.m.

nodes.text: The respondent denies that Kapil Luthra is using the shop as a godown or has taken exclusive possession of it

source_refs.quote: It is also denied that the alleged sub-lettee Sh. Kapil Luthra is using the shop in question as a godown and has taken exclusive possession of the same.

nodes.text: The respondent states that the shop was never sublet or assigned to Kapil Luthra and that the respondent uses the disputed shop as a godown

source_refs.quote: at no point of time, the shop in question was ever sublet or as- signed to Sh. Kapil Luthra.
the shop in dispute is being used by the Respondent as godown.

nodes.text: The respondent states that Kapil Luthra only helps in the family business and that no rent is received from him

source_refs.quote: Kapil Luthra is only helping the answering respondent in his family business and no rent as alleged is being received by the answering respondent from Sh. Kapil Luthra.

nodes.text: A respondent-side statement describes Kapil Luthra as the tenant's nephew who helps in the family business and states that the family remains in possession of the shop

source_refs.quote: "Sh. Kapil Luthra is the nephew of my client and he is helping my client in the family business and my family is very much in possession of the shop as a lawful tenant."

nodes.text: The record contains a claim that the shop is used as a godown for storing spare parts and cycles and that this use is within the petitioner's knowledge

source_refs.quote: shop is being used as a godown for storing spare parts, cycle etc. and the said fact is well within the knowledge of the petitioner.

source_refs.quote: If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself
A tenant cannot be said to part with the possession of any part of the premises unless his agreement with the license wholly ousts him from the legal possession of that part.
